prompt: Let $A$ be a set and $R\subseteq A\times A$ a binary relation on $A$. For $x,y\in A$, write $R(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in R$. Which condition defines transitivity?

answers.text: $\forall x\in A\;\forall y\in A\;\forall z\in A\; ((R(x,y)\land R(y,z))\Rightarrow R(x,z))$.
answers.explanation: Every two-step chain has its direct shortcut, including chains with repeated vertices.
Every element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. This defines reflexivity, not transitivity.
Every related pair has its reverse; loops are allowed but not required. This defines symmetry, not transitivity.

answers.text: $\forall x\in A\;\forall y\in A\; ((R(x,y)\land R(y,x))\Rightarrow x=y)$.
answers.explanation: Mutual relatedness forces equality. Self-loops are allowed. This defines antisymmetry, not transitivity.

answers.text: $\forall x\in A\;\forall y\in A\;\forall z\in A\; ((R(x,y)\land R(y,z))\Rightarrow\neg R(x,z))$.
answers.explanation: Every two-step chain lacks its direct shortcut. Failure of transitivity instead requires at least one chain without its shortcut. This defines antitransitivity, not transitivity.

answers.text: $\forall x\in A\;\forall y\in A\;\forall z\in A\; ((R(x,y)\land R(x,z))\Rightarrow R(y,z))$.
answers.explanation: Two outgoing neighbours of the same element must be related in the indicated direction. This defines the right-euclidean property, not transitivity.

answers.text: $\forall x\in A\;\forall y\in A\; (x\ne y\Rightarrow (R(x,y)\lor R(y,x)))$.
answers.explanation: Every pair of distinct elements is comparable in at least one direction. This convention imposes no condition on loops. This defines connexity on distinct elements, not transitivity.

answers.text: $\exists x\in A\;\exists y\in A\;\exists z\in A\; ((R(x,y)\land R(y,z))\land\neg R(x,z))$.
answers.explanation: Some two-step chain lacks its shortcut; other chains may have shortcuts. This defines failure of transitivity, not transitivity.

answers.text: $\forall x\in A\;\forall y\in A\;\forall z\in A\; ((R(x,y)\land R(x,z))\Rightarrow y=z)$.
answers.explanation: An element has at most one outgoing related element; it need not have any. This defines right-uniqueness, not transitivity.
Each element has at least one outgoing related element, which may be itself. This defines seriality, not transitivity.
